name: HITRUST CSF
full_name: HITRUST CSF readiness: HCG control set organized by the HITRUST assessment domains
issuing_body: Heights Consulting Group, organized on the HITRUST CSF assessment domains (HITRUST Alliance)
notice: HCG readiness control set for HITRUST CSF assessments. HITRUST CSF requirement statements, numbering and scoring are licensed by HITRUST Alliance and are not reproduced; controls here carry HCG numbering and are grouped by the HITRUST assessment domains. A HITRUST e1, i1 or r2 certification requires a validated assessment by an authorized external assessor submitted through HITRUST.

sources.title: HCG HITRUST readiness control set: domains, controls, guidance and test points

control_flags.type: hcg for an HCG-written readiness control.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable controls implemented, with partial implementation counting as half. HITRUST scores r2 requirements on maturity levels and i1 and e1 requirements on implementation; this percentage is an HCG readiness measure, not a HITRUST score.

rules.summary: A control is implemented only when every HCG test point under it is met.

All domains apply unless excluded from the assessment scope with justification; controls fully inherited from a service provider are marked met only when the provider's assurance evidence is obtained.
In the implementation score a partially implemented control counts as half. This is an HCG convention.

glossary.definition: A certifiable framework that harmonizes requirements from many standards and regulations, including HIPAA, NIST and ISO, maintained by HITRUST Alliance.
HITRUST's assessment types: e1 covers essential cybersecurity hygiene, i1 a broader leading-practice set, and r2 a risk-based, tailored set scored on maturity.
Relying on a service provider's validated HITRUST controls for part of the organization's own assessment.
A plan for remediating a requirement that did not meet the scoring threshold, with owner, actions and target date.
